intro.title: N-Queens
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a program that solves the N-Queens problem, which involves placing N chess queens on an N×N chessboard so that no two queens threaten each other. You will learn to implement a backtracking algorithm, a core programming concept that explores possible solutions step-by-step and undoes choices when they lead to a dead end. The main technologies involved are JavaScript arrays for representing the board and recursion for exploring placements. By the end, you'll understand how to systematically solve constraint-based problems using this fundamental algorithmic approach.
intro.usecase: The N-Queens backtracking algorithm pattern appears in real-world scheduling and resource allocation systems, such as conference room booking interfaces where multiple meetings must be placed without time conflicts. Product managers use similar constraint-solving logic in dashboard filters that prevent overlapping date ranges or mutually exclusive options. This pattern also powers interactive seating chart tools for events, ensuring guests are placed according to social distancing or grouping rules without violating proximity constraints.
